src/sysdolphin/baselib/fobj.c.value: Each FObj stores its interpreter state in the low nibble of flags while preserving the upper flag bits. Requesting animation rewinds the packed-data stream, initializes channel time from the descriptor start frame plus the requested frame, clears parser and interpolation working state, and enters state 1. Interpretation treats state 0 as inactive; states 1 and 2 load operations, state 3 loads a wait after optionally emitting a discrete key, states 4 and 5 alternate interpolation evaluation and boundary processing, and state 6 launches and emits discrete-key data. Stopping an FObj first flushes a pending discrete-key operation, then changes its state to 0.
src/sysdolphin/baselib/fobj.c.rationale: The state accessors, request and stop routines, and interpreter switch preserve the same representation and transitions at head.

evidence.why: Shows low-nibble state storage, request-time reset, entry into state 1, pending-key flushing, and transition to state 0 on stop.
